title: Artificial Intelligence Basics
description: Explore the principles of AI, the Turing Test, neural networks, computer vision, and modern GenAI.
seoTitle: Artificial Intelligence Basics Quiz – Test Your AI Knowledge | AI Quiz Arena
seoDescription: Test your AI knowledge with this 10-question quiz on neural networks, Turing test, generative AI, and computer vision.

questions.question: Who formulated the famous 1950 'Imitation Game' benchmark commonly known as the Turing Test?
questions.explanation: Alan Turing proposed the test in his seminal paper 'Computing Machinery and Intelligence' to evaluate machine conversational indistinguishability.

questions.question: What does the abbreviation 'LLM' stand for in contemporary AI technologies?
questions.explanation: Large Language Models (LLMs) are deep learning models trained on vast corpora of text capable of understanding and generating language.

questions.question: What computing architecture inspired by biological neurons forms the core of modern deep learning?
questions.explanation: Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) mimic interconnected biological brain neurons with weighted nodes and activation functions.

questions.question: Which field of AI enables computers to derive meaningful information from digital images and videos?
questions.explanation: Computer Vision equips algorithms to extract, analyze, and comprehend visual inputs such as photos and video feeds.

questions.question: Who is credited with coining the term 'Artificial Intelligence' at the 1956 Dartmouth workshop?
questions.explanation: John McCarthy proposed the term 'Artificial Intelligence' in the 1955 proposal for the historic 1956 Dartmouth Summer Research Project.

questions.question: What does 'NLP' stand for in artificial intelligence research?
questions.explanation: Natural Language Processing (NLP) is the branch of AI dedicated to giving computers the ability to understand text and spoken words.

questions.question: What is the phenomenon called when an AI model confidently invents false information or non-existent facts?
questions.explanation: Hallucination describes generative AI outputs that present factual inaccuracies or ungrounded claims with high stylistic confidence.

questions.question: Which company created the famous AlphaGo system that defeated world Go champion Lee Sedol in 2016?
questions.explanation: DeepMind developed AlphaGo, combining Monte Carlo tree search with deep neural networks to master the game of Go.

questions.question: What type of learning involves an agent receiving rewards or penalties based on its actions in an environment?
questions.explanation: Reinforcement Learning trains an agent to maximize cumulative rewards through trial-and-error environmental interactions.

questions.question: What is the revolutionary neural architecture introduced by Google researchers in the 2017 paper 'Attention Is All You Need'?
questions.explanation: The Transformer architecture relies on self-attention mechanisms and serves as the architectural foundation for modern LLMs.
